evidence:
All task-relative paths below refer to .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task/. Assigned workbook quality row 49 and internal annotation require every repeated runtime fact/literal to agree. Source-confirmed literal drift: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:34 instructs "If ID routing fails, retain that failure in hro_offer_identity" after the P4 approval/revision/rescission protocol. In contrast, tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:110 explicitly limits hro_offer_identity to creation and saved identity and says later approval, rescission and revision routing have separate owners; :114-128 define distinct approval and rescission routing criteria. The same criterion literal therefore has incompatible failure attribution between the executed shared protocol and its criterion.

Additional stale gate-state prose: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:11 says earlier gates may leave a "committed offer", while tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-26 require the gate offer to remain PENDING and forbid settlement. tests/gates/constraints/prompt.md:7 still says UI interactions for "requisition creation, offer creation and approval" despite :5 explicitly prohibiting approval. Those stale references are bounded ambiguity rather than evidence that an extra approval actually ran; the explicit pending-only gate criterion is clear.

The core repeated runtime facts otherwise agree on inspected current bytes: instruction.md:9, environment/instructions/integration.md:3-10 and tests/test.sh:97-112,164-168 use /app/server.js, port 3000, NODE_PATH, /app/app.db and DB_PATH; solution/app/src/bootstrap.js:42 and src/db.js:13 honor those overrides. All seven embedded seed families in functional/prompt.md:25 were parsed and compared field-by-field with public seed, resolving actor/referrer IDs to names: no mismatches; environment and solution seed bytes are identical. The 4-year annualization, band edges 200000/350000 dollars, vesting constants and referral figures agree with the public rules and sampled P3/P4/P6/P7/P8 calculations. task.toml:31-35 matches the frozen template judge environment; all five judge files fall back to claude-code. scoring.toml remains 0.6/0.2/0.2 with zero-weight gates and .05 floor and tools/score.py reads that file. counterexample: A partial implementation correctly creates and freshly retrieves every unusual offer ID, and supports ordinary-ID lifecycle operations, but its revision action constructs an unescaped path and fails on the P4 unusual ID. It satisfies hro_offer_identity as defined at judge.toml:110. Following prompt.md:34 instead would incorrectly remove that creation/readback credit for its separately owned lifecycle defect. This is a concrete source-level scoring counterexample, not an observed configured-judge result. A fully conforming alternate implementation using arbitrary routes and query-encoded IDs is permitted by the inspected contract; no conflicting port, account, date, route or arithmetic literal was found that would fail it. A dead-approval implementation is intentionally allowed past the pending-only gate and should lose only its separately observed functional outcomes; the stale approval prose must not enlarge that gate.
suggested_fix: Update P4 to attribute each ID-routing failure only to the owning lifecycle criterion while preserving successful creation/readback evidence; also replace the stale committed-gate wording with pending and remove approval from the constraints prompt interaction list.
